title: Continuum: Efficient and Robust Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache Time-to-Live
technique: KV cache time-to-live pinning across tool calls (TTL from reload cost and expected queueing delay) plus program-level FCFS scheduling

optimized_metrics.evidence: We present Continnum, a serving system to optimize job completion time for multi-turn agent workloads by introducing time-tolive mechanism for KV cache retention.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: improves the average job completion times by over

optimized_metrics.evidence: we can balance the benefit of cache reuse against the ... need to maintain system throughput for other requests to achieve
per-turn queueing delay. ... This per-turn queueing delay can accumulate and result in increasing delay for each agentic program

headline_claim.text: Continnum improves the average job completion times by over 8x while improving throughput.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 8-10, 12-15 (Average Job Delay / Average Job Duration)
Jobs Per Second (JPS) axes, Fig 8-10; steps per minute in Table

metric_definitions.term_as_written: job completion time / Average Job Delay / per-job finish time
metric_definitions.definition_quote: Both the benefit and the cost are measured in units of time, since they ultimately translate into changes in the total job completion latency across all programs.
metric_definitions.notes: Job = an agent program (multi-turn ReAct loop of LLM calls plus tool calls). 'Job Delay'/'Job Duration' used on plot axes without a separate formal definition; Fig 12 text: 'We measure the per-job finish time'. Job completion includes tool execution time (traces replayed) and queueing across turns.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: When the next inference step has its KV cache evicted from GPU memory, even if the KV cache can be reloaded from CPU, it will also have to wait in the waiting queue for other requests to free up GPU memory before starting inference.
metric_definitions.notes: Queueing delay that accumulates per turn; the key quantity the TTL cost model estimates.
Used as the offered job arrival rate (x-axis, Poisson arrivals); the 'throughput' improvement is read from the rate at which delay blows up. Not formally defined in text.

load_regime: trace replay of SWE-Bench, BFCL V4, OpenHands agent traces with job-per-second (Poisson) arrival-rate sweep
tradeoff_acknowledged: Pinned KV can occupy GPU memory and deadlock the scheduler (handled by unpinning); retention costs memory for other requests (cost term in utility model). Autellix underperforms on SWE-Bench.
hardware: A100-SXM, H100, B200; Company A internal H100 testbed
workloads: SWE-Bench (mini-swe-agent traces), BFCL V4 web search, OpenHands, multi-SWE-bench; real SWE-agent run on SWE-bench-Verified
extractor_notes: Program-level (job) completion time is the stated objective; request-level TTFT/TPOT not used. Mean primary, P90/P95 secondary.
